text: Regional indicators (U+1F1E6-U+1F1FF): when the next code point is a regional indicator, the indicators immediately before it are counted by stepping back 2 code units at a time from pos - 2; an odd count joins the indicator (pair completed), an even count breaks. text: Backward from pos > 1: for candidate c = pos - 2, pos - 3, ... it computes the forward break from c and returns the first result that is lower than the current candidate pos (the loop variable decremented each step), else 0. text: A tab (code unit 9) moves the column to the next multiple of tabSize: n += tabSize - (n % tabSize); a tab at a tab stop advances a full tabSize. The tab is stepped by one code unit (i++).

Every other grapheme cluster counts one column, found with findClusterBreak(string, i) (includeExtending true): an astral code point (2 units), a base with marks, a ZWJ sequence, a flag pair, a wide CJK character and each of CR, LF, U+2028 all count 1. There is no East Asian width and no zero-width case; Hangul jamo count one each (findClusterBreak B9).

A `to` that falls inside a cluster (between surrogate halves, between a base and its mark) counts that whole cluster: the test i < to is made at the cluster start. `to` inside a tab is not possible (a tab is one unit); `to` = 0 is column 0.
hazards: A `to` inside a character is accepted; its column is that of the end of the cluster (D1).

text: A Line is a plain object with four data fields (from, to, number, text) and a length getter, created by Text.lineAt and Text.line on every call: two queries for the same line return distinct objects (doc.line(1) !== doc.line(1)), so Line identity carries no meaning. Its constructor is @internal; instanceof Line holds for every returned value.
hazards: Object identity: a fresh object per query; no caller may rely on ===.
Fields are writable at runtime (TypeScript readonly only); length is recomputed from them (F0822).
stack: Mechanism: lines are not stored as objects; a Line is allocated per query (doc comment "It is created on-demand when lines are queried", mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:560-561). Editor need underneath: describing a line without storing per-line objects in a large document. Allocation per call relies on a garbage collector (deduction).
cost: O(log n) per query (the lookup); the object itself O(1) plus a reference to the stored line string

text: Position of the first code unit of the line, in UTF-16 code units: 0 for line 1, and the previous line's to + 1 for every later line (each line break takes exactly one position, whatever separator the source text used). Astral characters count 2 positions; CR and U+2028 stored inside a line are ordinary content.
Position at the end of the line's content, before its line break: from + text.length in UTF-16 code units.
For the last line, to equals the document length (there is no break after it); for an empty last line from == to == length.

1-based line number: 1 for the first line, lines for the last; from lineAt(pos) it is the number of breaks before pos plus one, where a pos at a line's end (just before its break) belongs to that line.
The line's content without any line break, the same string the document stores (no copy is made); "" for an empty line. CR and U+2028 inside a line given to Text.of are content.
hazards: Aliasing: the string is the stored one (immutable in JS, so not observable).

text: Three implementations share the interface: the raw cursor (Text.iter), the partial cursor (Text.iterRange) and the line cursor (Text.iterLines). Each is its own iterable: [Symbol.iterator]() returns the cursor itself, so for..of and spread continue from the current state and a second spread yields nothing. next() returns the cursor itself, which serves as the iterator-protocol result object ({value, done}).
hazards: Duck-typed protocol: the cursor is its own IteratorResult; the same object is returned by every next().
Mutable shared state: iterating with for..of consumes the cursor.
stack: Mechanism: the cursor doubles as the JS IteratorResult and is installed on prototypes only when Symbol exists (`if (typeof Symbol != "undefined")`, mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:554). Evidence: that guard (backward compatibility with engines without Symbol) and the structure; no CHANGELOG entry found. Editor need underneath: sequential reading of the document.

text: Before the first next(): value is "", done is false, lineBreak is false, for all three cursors and both directions.

Raw forward cursor (iter() or iter(1)), next() without skip: yields each non-empty line's whole content and "
" for each line break, in document order, then done. Empty lines yield nothing of their own (two consecutive breaks show as two "
"); the empty document is done at the first call. Values never span a line break; a "
" stored inside a line (Q9) is part of a line value with lineBreak false. Whole lines are returned, never split at leaf or node boundaries.
hazards: Empty lines produce no value: callers count positions from value lengths (DocInput, lint, view) and see breaks only.
cost: amortized O(1) per value (a stack of nodes, one entry per tree level)

text: Raw reverse cursor (iter(-1)): yields the same values in reverse order (the strings themselves are not reversed): last line first, "\n" for each break, empty lines skipped.

Raw cursor, next(skip) with skip > 0: the cursor's position p is the end of the previous value (forward; the start for reverse), 0 (length for reverse) before the first call. Forward it reads at q = p + skip: done (value "") when q >= length; "\n" when q is a line-break position; otherwise the rest of the line from q (which can start or end inside a surrogate pair, giving a lone surrogate, F0843). Reverse reads at q = p - skip: done when q <= 0; "\n" when q - 1 is a break; otherwise the part of the line before q. Skips cross whole tree children without visiting them when skip exceeds the child's length. Checked against this model on 300 seeded cases (gen-text.ts).
hazards: UTF-16: a skip can land inside a surrogate pair and the value then starts or ends with a lone surrogate.

text: Raw cursor, next(skip) with skip < 0: implemented as one step of |skip| positions in the opposite direction and a step forward over that value's length (nextInner(-skip, -dir) then nextInner(value.length, dir)); the observable result is the same model with q = max(0, p + skip) forward (min(length, p - skip) reverse): next(-k) after a value ending at p returns the rest of the line from p - k, or "\n" at a break; skipping before the start clamps to the start (next(-1000) returns the first line). A negative skip after done reads again (done becomes false, F0853); as the first call, next(-1) reads from 0 (F0851).
hazards: done is not sticky under a negative skip on the raw cursor.

text: After the end: next() with skip >= 0 keeps returning done true and value "" on all three cursors. A negative skip after done differs per cursor: the raw cursor reads again (done false, F0853); the partial cursor stays done (F0854); the line cursor sets value to the inner value but keeps done true (value "b" with done true, F0855).
hazards: LineCursor.done is set once and never reset: after done, a negative skip leaves done true with a non-empty value.

text: Partial cursor (iterRange(from, to)), next() without skip: yields the raw cursor's values clipped to [min(from, to), max(from, to)): the first value starts at from (forward) and the last ends at to; with from > to it runs in reverse over [to, from); from == to is done at once. The range is not clipped to the document (Text.iterRange B2). done is set when a step produces an empty value (done = !value). Values can start or end inside a surrogate pair (F0864).
hazards: UTF-16: range ends inside a surrogate pair give lone surrogates.

text: Partial cursor, forward, next(skip) after the first step: skip > 0 is clipped to to - pos, skip < 0 to from - pos, so the cursor stays inside the range (next(100) past the end gives done, next(-5) back to from returns the piece at from, F0868). On the first call a negative skip is clipped with max(skip, from - pos) where from - pos is positive (pos is 0 before the first step), so it becomes a forward skip of from and the cursor reads at 2 * from instead of from (iterRange(2, 12).next(-5) returns "two" at 4, F0869; text-s2-q2).
hazards: Skip clipping uses forward bounds before the first step (text-s2-q2).

text: Partial cursor, reverse (from > to), next(skip) with skip != 0: the clipping in next() uses the forward bounds (min(skip, to - pos), max(skip, from - pos)) whatever the direction. Before the first step pos is the document length, so to - pos is negative and a positive skip turns into a negative one: iterRange(12, 2).next(2) returns "four" (positions 15-19, outside the range), iterRange(6, 2) on "abcdefgh" with next(1) returns "cdefgh" (positions 2-8), iterRange(8, 2).next(1) ignores the skip (F0870, F0872, F0873). After the first step a positive skip is limited by the distance already travelled (to - pos) rather than the distance left, and a negative skip by from - pos (F0871). text-s2-q2.

text: Line cursor (iterLines), next() without skip: yields each line's content once, "" for every empty line including empty lines at the end of the range and the single line of the empty document, never "\n"; then done. Implemented over an inner raw or partial cursor: a break directly after a line is consumed by a recursive next(), a break after a break (or at the start) yields "", and the end after a break yields one final "" (CHANGELOG 6.3.2, mirrors/cm6/state/CHANGELOG.md:113).
hazards: Recursion: next() calls itself once per line break (depth 1).

text: Line cursor, next(skip): the skip is passed to the inner cursor unchanged, so values can be partial lines (iterLines().next(1) on "one" gives "ne"); a skip landing on a line-break position yields "" as if an empty line followed (F0881); negative skips read backward through the inner raw cursor (F0882).

The current string: "" before the first next() and whenever done is true (except the line cursor after a negative skip past the end, TextIterator.next B5); otherwise a line or part of one, or "\n" for a break on raw and partial cursors; on a line cursor "" also stands for an empty line.
hazards: On a line cursor value "" with done false is an empty line; on raw and partial cursors value "" only comes with done true.

text: false until a next() finds nothing more, then true with value "". Raw cursor: set when the root's end (start in reverse) is reached and cleared at the start of every step; partial cursor: set when the position reaches the bound or a step produces an empty value; line cursor: set on the inner cursor's second done (the first one after a break yields a final ""), never cleared.
hazards: Line cursor done is sticky even when value changes afterwards (TextIterator.next B5).

text: Raw cursor: true exactly when the current value is a "\n" produced by a line break (cleared at every step, false when done). Partial cursor: a getter, true when the inner raw cursor is at a break and the clipped value is not "" (false at done and for an empty range). Line cursor: a getter that is always false.
hazards: lineBreak is a field on one class and a getter on the others (prototype dispatch).

text: Text is an immutable value: replace, append and slice return new documents and leave the receiver unchanged; they never return the receiver itself, even for a no-op (doc.replace(0, 0, Text.empty), doc.append(Text.empty) and doc.slice(0) are all !== doc, for leaf and node documents, F0885). Unchanged parts are shared between the old and new trees (Text.replace B4, Text.slice B3).
hazards: Identity: a no-op edit still yields a new object, so identity does not signal "unchanged"; eq compares content.
stack: Mechanism: structural sharing between versions, which consumers exploit through object identity (autocomplete word.ts:19-49 caches per child Text in a WeakMap, Q8). Evidence: code structure (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:274, :293-295). Editor need underneath: cheap snapshots of a large document for undo history and transactions; the identity-keyed cache relies on garbage collection.

text: Two concrete classes behind the abstract Text: a leaf (constructor name TextLeaf) holding up to 32 line strings with the breaks implied between them, and a node (TextNode) holding child Texts with a break implied between consecutive children; both are instanceof Text. The constructor is protected and the subclasses are not exported, so documents come only from Text.of, Text.empty and the operations.
hazards: instanceof dispatch between TextLeaf and TextNode (replace, scanIdentical, TextNode.from, RawTextCursor).
Tree shape is observable through Text.children (Q8).
stack: Mechanism: a B-tree of line arrays with branch factor 2^5 (Tree.BranchShift, mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:1-7). Evidence: the const enum and the comments at mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:163-165, :247-250. Editor need underneath: logarithmic line lookup and edits on large documents; not a stack constraint.

text: Text.of with at most 32 lines keeps the caller's array as the leaf's storage without copying, while the length is computed once: mutating the array afterwards changes the document's lines (lines getter, toJSON, lineAt results) but not its length, leaving an inconsistent object (a = ["ab"]; t = Text.of(a); a[0] = "abcdef"; a.push("zz") gives length 2, lines 2, toString "ab", toJSON ["abcdef", "zz"], F0887). With more than 32 lines the lines are copied into new leaves (F0888); toJSON returns a fresh array (F0889).
hazards: Aliasing: the input array is stored by reference for documents of <= 32 lines.
Cached length vs live line array.
stack: Mechanism: no defensive copy of the input array. Evidence: code structure (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:156); no comment. Avoids a copy in a single-threaded JS program where callers are trusted not to mutate (deduction).

text: Number of positions: the sum of the line lengths in UTF-16 code units plus one per line break (lines - 1); 0 for the empty document, 1 for two empty lines, 2 for one astral character. Stored when the object is built (leaf: computed from the lines or passed in; node: passed in by the operation), never recomputed.
hazards: Cached value: stays stale if a leaf's aliased array is mutated (Text B3).
Can be fractional or NaN after operations with fractional or NaN positions (Text.replace B6, F0948, F0956).

text: Number of lines, >= 1 for every document built from valid arguments: the length of the leaf's array (a getter) or the sum of the children's lines, computed in the node constructor. A stored line containing "\n" counts as one line (Q9). A slice with a NaN position can produce a document with 0 lines (F0977).
hazards: Arguments outside the domain (Q9).
Leaf lines is live over the aliased array, node lines is cached (Text B3, Text.children B3).

text: pos < 0 or pos > length throws RangeError with the message `Invalid position ${pos} in document of length ${length}` (also for -0.5, 14.5 and Infinity, which fail the comparison). Callers can check 0 <= pos <= length in advance.
hazards: Exception with a message that formats the JS number (RangeError).

text: Returns the line containing pos: the first line whose to >= pos, so a pos at a line's end (just before its break) belongs to that line, pos = to + 1 starts the next line, and pos = length returns the last line. Positions count UTF-16 code units and one per break.
cost: O(log n) levels, with a linear scan of the children at each level (63 top-level children for 2000 lines, F1065) and of up to 32 lines in the leaf

text: A pos inside a character (between the halves of a surrogate pair) is accepted and returns the containing line; no snapping.
hazards: Positions inside a character are valid inputs (D1).

text: Empty document: lineAt(0) is {from 0, to 0, number 1, text ""}.

Non-integer positions that pass the range check (Q9): a fractional pos returns the first line whose to >= pos (lineAt(3.5) on "one\ntwo..." is line 2, lineAt(0.5) line 1); NaN passes both comparisons and the leaf scan runs off its array, throwing TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')".
hazards: Arguments outside the domain (Q9).
TypeError instead of RangeError for NaN.

text: Node documents: a pos equal to the end of a child (the position just before the break between two children) resolves in that child, giving its last line; pos + 1 gives the next child's first line (F0920, b = 3231 for 200 lines of 100 characters).

n < 1 or n > lines throws RangeError with the message `Invalid line number ${n} in ${lines}-line document` (also 0.5, 4.5 on a 4-line document and Infinity). Callers can check 1 <= n <= lines in advance.
hazards: Exception with a formatted message (RangeError).

text: Returns line n (1-based) with its from, to, number and text.

Non-integer line numbers in range (Q9): a fractional n returns the first line whose number >= n (line(1.5) is line 2, line(3.2) is line 4) with an integer number field; NaN throws TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')".

text: from and to are clipped first: from = max(0, min(length, from)), to = max(from, min(length, to)). A reversed range (from > to) becomes the empty range at from (an insertion), positions before 0 or after the end are pulled to the document bounds (replace(20, 30) appends, replace(-10, -5) prepends, F0946, F0947). The resulting length is computed from the clipped range (fixed in 6.3.3, mirrors/cm6/state/CHANGELOG.md:105). Fractional positions pass the clip unchanged (replace(2.5, 4) gives length 13.5, F0948; B6).

text: Content: the result is the text before from, then the inserted Text, then the text after to; the inserted text's first line is joined to the line at from and its last line to the line at to, so lines = this.lines - (breaks in [from, to)) + text.lines - 1. Inserting Text.of(["", ""]) inserts one break. Positions inside a surrogate pair split it, leaving lone surrogates in the lines (F0939). Checked against a string model on seeded cases (gen-text.ts).
hazards: UTF-16: replacing inside a surrogate pair produces ill-formed line strings.

text: Node receiver fast path: when the inserted text has fewer lines than the receiver and [from, to] lies inside one child (from >= child start and to <= child end, so a range ending exactly at a child end counts), the child is replaced recursively; when the updated child's line count stays strictly between totalLines >> 6 and totalLines >> 4 (totalLines being the new document's line count), the result is a node whose children array is a copy with only that child replaced, every other child shared by identity with the receiver (F0950, F0951); otherwise the receiver's replace runs the general path on that child's whole range with the updated child as the inserted text.

Structural sharing: untouched children are the same objects in both versions.
stack: Mechanism: copying only the path from the root to the edited leaf (comment "Fast path: if the change only affects one child and the child's size remains in the acceptable range, only update that child", mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:285-287). cost: O(depth * children per node + 32) for a local edit

text: General path (Text.replace): the receiver's part before from, the inserted text and the part after to are decomposed into a flat list of whole children and cut leaves, cut leaves at the two seams joined line-to-line (a joined leaf over 32 lines is split at half), then rebuilt by TextNode.from: fewer than 32 lines in total gives one flat leaf; otherwise chunk = max(32, lines >> 5), children over 2 * chunk lines are opened, children over chunk / 2 lines stand alone, adjacent small leaves merge while their total stays <= 32 lines, and the rest group into nodes of at most chunk lines. Whole children inside the kept ranges, including children of the inserted Text, are reused by identity. Shapes recorded: deleting all but 20 positions of 200 lines gives one leaf (F0952); ten 600-character inserts into a line keep [32 x 6, 8] (F0953); inserting 500 one-character lines gives F0954; 1999 appends give 59 leaves and one nested node (F0955).
hazards: Tree shape is observable through Text.children (Q8).
instanceof checks in TextNode.from (:345, :350-351).
Closures add/flush over mutable locals in TextNode.from (:342-368).
cost: O(log n * children per node) for the decomposition plus O(lines inserted / 32) for new leaves; the receiver is never materialized as a string
